calls.head: One power play bites, one doesn’t
calls.body: On the power play, Florida is near the top of the league, but Buffalo is near the bottom. Every penalty the Sabres take could cost them. These two hand each other plenty of power plays, so special teams should get a real say.
calls.call: The Panthers’ power play creates more per 60 than the Sabres’.

calls.title: Florida had the better chances
calls.plain: The Panthers made the better chances on the power play, as the gap between these two suggested, but the goals came out even. On the scoreboard: Florida 2 for 4, Buffalo 2 for 5 on the power play.
calls.said: the Panthers’ power play would make more chances than the Sabres’
calls.beyond: Florida has a better power play than most. Even by those standards, this was a big night: 39.5 expected goals per 60 on the power play, against their usual 8.0 and a league average of 7.6. A team strays this far less than once in a thousand games. You may never see it again.

calls.head: Where the Panthers have the edge: physicality
calls.body: The Panthers are the league’s best for physicality, and the Sabres are near the bottom. It’s the widest gap between these two, though not a huge one.
calls.call: The Panthers hit more than the Sabres in the close stretches of the game.

surprises.head: Both teams played to type
surprises.body: Nothing in this game strayed far from how these two usually play: the shot share, the quality of chances, special teams, hitting, ice time and goaltending all landed inside their normal night-to-night range.

story.head: The Sabres beat the Panthers
paras: Josh Doan got the scoring started for the Sabres early in the first, but Anton Lundell made it 1-1 for Florida midway through the period. Rasmus Dahlin restored the Sabres’ lead on the power play just under five minutes later. Florida pulled Jacob Markström after two goals and turned to Akira Schmid to start the second. Dahlin left early in the second period and didn’t return. The next day, he was listed as day to day with an upper-body injury. Sam Reinhart made it 2-2 for Florida on the power play early in the period. Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen took over from Colten Ellis in net for Buffalo for the rest of the second. Ryan McLeod put the Sabres back ahead 3-2 midway through the second. Reinhart scored again on the power play a little over two minutes later to tie it 3-3, but that was the last goal the Panthers would get. Noah Östlund put the Sabres ahead for good on the power play early in the third, and Tage Thompson made it 5-3 with less than seven minutes left.
Nothing much separated these two on the chances. This one could have gone either way. The Sabres moved to 3-3-0 and took fifth place in the Atlantic from the Panthers, who fell to 2-2-2.
